jp: お手洗[てあら]いは二階[にかい]に{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: The restroom is on the second floor.
why: For the existence of a thing, formal ございます replaces あります; おる and いらっしゃる are for people.

jp: こちらが当店[とうてん]のメニュー{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Here is our menu.
why: A noun statement 'this is X' becomes でございます in formal service speech.

jp: お探[さが]しの本[ほん]は三階[さんがい]に{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: The book you are looking for is on the third floor.
why: A book is a thing, so its location is ございます; おります and いらっしゃいます are for people, and でございます cannot follow に.

jp: 私[わたし]が担当[たんとう]の田中[たなか]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: I am Tanaka, the person in charge.
why: Speaking of myself I use humble-polite でございます; でいらっしゃいます would honour myself.

jp: 恐[おそ]れ入[い]りますが、ただいま在庫[ざいこ]が{ございません|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: I'm sorry, but we have no stock at the moment.
why: The negative of ございます is ございません; stock is a thing, so おる and いらっしゃる do not fit.

jp: 本日[ほんじつ]のおすすめは、この魚[さかな]料理[りょうり]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Today's recommendation is this fish dish.
why: 'X is Y' needs the copula, so でございます, not the existence verb ございます.

jp: ご質問[しつもん]が{ございましたら|kg-gozaimasu}、お知[し]らせください。
en: If you have any questions, please let us know.
d: いらっしゃいましたら
why: A question is not a person, so ございます is the formal 'there is'; the conditional form is ございましたら.

jp: こちらは新[あたら]しいパスポートの申請[しんせい]窓口[まどぐち]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: This is the counter for new passport applications.
why: Identifying what something is takes the copula, so でございます.

jp: 駐車場[ちゅうしゃじょう]は建物[たてもの]の裏[うら]に{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: The car park is behind the building.
why: A place where something exists is ございます in formal speech; the car park is not a person.

jp: ご注文[ちゅうもん]は以上[いじょう]{でございますか|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Is that all for your order?
why: The order is identified as 'that's all', which needs the copula でございます.

jp: お忘[わす]れ物[もの]が{ございました|kg-gozaimasu}ので、お預[あず]かりしています。
en: A forgotten item was found, so we are keeping it for you.
why: A lost item exists as a thing, so past ございました; おる and いらっしゃる are only for people.

jp: お支払[しはら]いは現金[げんきん]のみ{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Payment is by cash only.
why: 'Payment is cash only' is a noun statement, so でございます.

jp: あいにく、そちらのお部屋[へや]はすでに満室[まんしつ]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Unfortunately, that room is already fully booked.
why: The state 'is fully booked' is stated with the formal copula でございます.

jp: こちらの商品[しょうひん]には保証書[ほしょうしょ]が{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: This product comes with a warranty.
why: A warranty exists as a thing, so the formal existence verb ございます.

jp: お電話[でんわ]ありがとうございます。山田[やまだ]商事[しょうじ]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Thank you for calling. This is Yamada Trading.
why: Answering the phone 'This is Yamada Trading' uses the copula でございます.

jp: お席[せき]は窓[まど]側[がわ]と奥[おく]の二[ふた]つ{ございますが|kg-gozaimasu}、どちらがよろしいですか。
en: We have two seats, one by the window and one at the back. Which would you prefer?
why: Seats are things that exist, so ございます; the others are for people or need a noun before them.

jp: ご不明[ふめい]な点[てん]は{ございませんか|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Is there anything that is unclear to you?
d: いらっしゃいませんか
why: The existence of a point (a thing) is asked with ございませんか in formal service speech.

jp: こちらが今日[きょう]の日替[ひが]わり定食[ていしょく]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: This is today's set meal of the day.
why: Presenting what a dish is takes the copula でございます.

jp: 会議室[かいぎしつ]には、プロジェクターが{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: The meeting room has a projector.
why: A projector is an object, so its existence is ございます.

jp: お客様[きゃくさま]のお荷物[にもつ]は、こちらの二点[にてん]{でございますね|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Your luggage is these two items, correct?
why: 'The luggage is these two items' is a noun statement, so でございます plus ね.

jp: 当店[とうてん]では、傘[かさ]の貸[か]し出[だ]しも{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: We also offer umbrella lending at our shop.
why: A service that exists in the shop is ございます, the formal あります.

jp: 当店[とうてん]には、お子様[こさま]向[む]けのメニューも{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: We also have a menu for children.
why: A menu is a thing, so the formal existence verb ございます is used.

jp: お探[さが]しの靴[くつ]は、あいにくそのサイズが{ございません|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: I'm afraid we don't have the shoes you are looking for in that size.
why: A size is not a person, so the negative of formal ある is ございません.

jp: ご予約[よやく]のお名前[なまえ]は、佐藤様[さとうさま]{でございますね|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: The name on the reservation is Mr. Sato, correct?
why: Confirming 'the name is X' uses the copula, so でございますね.

jp: この先[さき]に、小[ちい]さな展望台[てんぼうだい]が{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Up ahead there is a small observation deck.
why: An observation deck is a thing that exists, so ございます.

jp: 午前[ごぜん]の便[びん]は、すでに満席[まんせき]{でございました|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: The morning flight was already full.
why: 'Was full' is a noun-state statement, so past でございました, not ございました alone.

jp: お客様[きゃくさま]にお知[し]らせが{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: We have an announcement for our customers.
why: An announcement exists as a thing, so ございます in formal announcement style.

jp: 本日[ほんじつ]の営業[えいぎょう]は午後[ごご]八時[はちじ]まで{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Today we are open until eight in the evening.
why: 'Business is until eight' is a noun statement, so でございます.

jp: エレベーターは、あちらの角[かど]を曲[ま]がったところに{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: The elevator is just around that corner.
why: The location of a thing in formal speech is ございます.

jp: ご希望[きぼう]の日[ひ]に空[あ]きが{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: We have availability on the day you would like.
why: Availability is not a person, so formal existence ございます.

jp: こちらは禁煙席[きんえんせき]{でございますが|kg-gozaimasu}、よろしいでしょうか。
en: This is a non-smoking seat; is that all right?
why: 'This is a non-smoking seat' identifies the seat, so でございますが.

jp: 館内[かんない]には、無料[むりょう]の自動販売機[じどうはんばいき]が{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: There is a free vending machine inside the building.
why: A vending machine is a thing, so ございます is the formal existence verb.

jp: 先日[せんじつ]の件[けん]で、少[すこ]しご相談[そうだん]が{ございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: I have something I would like to consult you about regarding the other day.
why: A matter to consult about is a thing that exists, so ございます.

jp: お会計[かいけい]は一万円[いちまんえん]{でございます|kg-gozaimasu}。
en: Your bill comes to ten thousand yen.
why: A price statement 'it is X yen' takes the copula でございます.
